Prevention: Keep fallow land free of seasonal host plants
Synchronize early planting so that the insect does not find and infect young plants to build up its population
Remove all alternate hosts (grass family) and wild rice from the field and field boundaries
Apply proper fertilizer doses to avoid over-dose as this would cause profuse leaf formation
Monitoring: Check for elongate-tubular eggs (laid singly) and maggot-like larva feeding inside developing buds.
Look for stunted plants with deformed, wilted, and rolled leaves
Look for elongated leaf sheaths, also called onion leaf or silvershoot
Monitor affected tillers which inhibits growth of leaves and fails to produce panicles
Take action when 30% of plants have typical symptom or 5-10 adult flies are seen on the crop
Direct Control: Handpick and destroy egg masses at the nursery and at transplanting
Remove and destroy the onion/silvery shoots
Apply pesticides judiciously to conserve pteromalid wasps (that parasitize the larvae), phytoseiid mites (feed on eggs), spiders (feed on adults)
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
